Definition: People take greater risks when safety measures reduce perceived danger.
Ex1: After buying a helmet, he cycled faster through traffic-filled downtown streets.
Ex2: Drivers sped more once anti-lock brakes made them feel safer.
Ex3: She texted while walking because sidewalks now had protective railings.
Ex4: Wearing masks, partygoers ignored distancing rules at crowded indoor events.
Ex5: Insurance coverage encouraged riskier skiing on unfamiliar, icy mountain slopes.
C-Ex1: Even with airbags, she drives cautiously and obeys every traffic signal.
C-Ex2: He still follows safety protocols despite advanced protective laboratory equipment.
C-Ex3: Lifeguards increased vigilance after new flotation devices were installed.

Definition: People adjust behavior, increasing risk, when they feel more protected.

C-Ex2: He maintained slow driving even after upgrading vehicle safety systems.
C-Ex3: She studied harder despite knowing partial credit was guaranteed.
